# Astra Spec Claude Build

Carry the request through specification, implementation, independent reviews, verification and a published PR. A build invocation authorizes scoped commits, task-branch pushes and a PR, not merging or deployment. Editing this skill alone does not start that workflow. Explicit user model choices override automatic routing.

## Model assignments

| Role | Model | Reasoning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workflow coordinator | GPT-5.6 Terra (`gpt-5.6-terra`) for bounded work; GPT-5.6 Sol (`gpt-5.6-sol`) for uncertain or high-consequence coordination | low by default; medium when task evidence requires it |
| Spec author and decision owner | GPT-6 Astra (`gpt-6-astra`) | medium |
| Spec and first code reviewer | Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`), subscription CLI | provider default |
| Bounded implementation | Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5`) | high |
| Complex implementation | Opus 5 (`claude-opus-5`) | high |
| Final independent reviewer | GPT-6 Astra (`gpt-6-astra`), fresh context | high |

Astra owns specification and review adjudication; the selected builder applies implementation and accepted fixes. The coordinator manages stage transitions, workers, checks, preservation and publication without retaining specification work in its own context. Delegate specification/adjudication to Astra at the exact model and effort above. Never simulate another model's role by labeling your own output.

## Usage discipline

Treat model calls as work units, not as a monitoring loop. The normal path is one Astra specification, one Fable spec review, one builder session, one Fable code review and one fresh Astra final review. Start an additional model run only when a concrete finding, failed acceptance criterion, material base change or interrupted session invalidates an earlier result; record that trigger in the handoff. Repeated related failures trigger the architectural root-cause check; do not spend repeated model calls patching symptoms before that check is complete. Do not create parallel agents for the same role, keep completed agents alive for status, or ask a model to restate evidence already preserved in an artifact.

Use GPT-5.6 Terra at low reasoning for routine coordination with accepted requirements and clear checks. Increase Terra to medium when coordination must reconcile several dependent slices. Use GPT-5.6 Sol at medium for uncertain cross-system integration, consequential conflict resolution or recovery where the coordinator itself must reason about coupled invariants. Return to Terra after the decision is settled. Do not use Astra as the persistent root coordinator merely because Astra authors the specification or adjudicates findings.

Keep stage contexts narrow. Give each worker the accepted spec, current snapshot and only the repository material needed for its role. Prefer compact durable handoffs over conversation replay. Start fresh reviewer contexts as already required, and start a fresh coordinator task for a new coherent slice instead of carrying an unrelated build history forward.

Supervise through process state, exit status, filesystem changes and event-driven waits. Stream activity locally without sending each update through a model. Batch independent read-only inspections and related checks. Avoid repeated unchanged status reads and fragmented command calls made only to narrate progress. When an approval is required, prepare the exact scoped action first and request a reusable narrow command prefix when appropriate; do not generate repeated approval-review traffic for equivalent commands.

Scale specifications and verification to risk. A bounded change still receives all required roles, but its spec, acceptance matrix and test set should remain concise. One successful relevant check is enough unless changed code, a review finding or unresolved evidence requires another run. Do not broaden tests, reviews or research after the acceptance criteria are demonstrated.

Assess uncertainty, interacting systems, consequences of error and available verification—not just file count or whether the work is called a test fix. Record the selected exact model, effort, reason and escalation trigger in the handoff before dispatch.

| Task evidence | Builder |
| --- | --- |
| Accepted design, established local pattern, bounded change and clear checks: ordinary feature wiring, straightforward bug with known cause, mechanical refactor, docs or fixture repair | Sonnet 5 |
| Uncertain root cause; cross-owner state changes; concurrency, retries or transaction semantics; privacy/consent/data-loss risks; behavioral merge conflicts; broad refactoring or long autonomous investigation | Opus 5 |
| Mixed feature | Opus 5 for the hard boundary, then Sonnet 5 for independent well-specified slices after the decision is settled |

Start bounded work with Sonnet 5; escalate if inspection reveals coupled invariants or if a meaningful attempted correction still fails the same acceptance criterion. Do not spend repeated cheaper-model turns circling an unresolved correctness problem. A test failure alone is not proof of a model limitation: distinguish environment, fixture, permission and implementation failures. Return to Sonnet 5 at a checkpoint when uncertainty is resolved and remaining work is bounded. Keep high effort initially; adjust only for measured task evidence and supported settings, never automatically use maximum effort. Evaluate outcomes with the real task's tests and independent reviews.

This routing applies Anthropic's guidance to this repository: Sonnet for everyday coding balancing speed and capability, Opus for complex agentic coding and systems work; benchmark actual tasks before changing the balance. The concrete risk examples above are local policy, not vendor guarantees. Sources checked September 11, 2026: [Choosing a model](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/choosing-a-model), [Models overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview). Give Fable 5.1 the user request, spec, and repository access. Ask it to audit feasibility, intended behavior, missing journeys, incorrect assumptions, unnecessary complexity, data consistency, proposed tests, unclear ownership, duplicate producers or consumers, missing durable outcome states, retry-identity gaps, and delayed-work reversals of terminal actions. Require concrete counterexamples and file references where applicable.

Astra evaluates each finding as accepted, rejected with evidence, or unresolved. Route applicable ownership findings through the architectural root-cause check, then revise the spec for accepted findings. Re-review with Fable when revisions change architecture, user behavior, migrations, or important acceptance criteria, or when the first review left substantive uncertainty. A wording-only change does not require another pass.

Default to at most three substantive review/revision rounds per stage. If material disagreement persists, summarize the exact decision needed and pause the dependent work rather than looping indefinitely or treating the review as passed.

Confirmed in-scope correctness, privacy, data-loss, security, and acceptance failures block completion. Missing required verification or a required model review also blocks a claim of completion. Cosmetic preferences and unrelated improvements are optional and should not restart review cycles. Investigate speculative concerns until they can be supported or rejected with evidence; model disagreement alone is not a blocker. At the round limit, escalate only a specific unresolved material issue and continue any independent work that remains valid.

### Attach the agreed spec to Linear

After Astra resolves the spec review and the spec satisfies any repository-required readiness gate, attach the exact agreed spec to the task's Linear ticket **before implementation**. Keep the durable spec in the repository and record its path and content hash in the handoff. Make the complete Markdown spec readable in Linear: append or update a clearly delimited `Accepted specification` section in the ticket description, preserving the original request and unrelated content. A local filesystem path alone is not an attachment. If using a native file attachment instead, verify that the uploaded document is accessible from the ticket.

With the bundled CLI, read/export the existing description, compose the merged description in a durable task file, then use the supported `set-desc <IDENT> <file>` and `verify-desc <IDENT> <file>` commands. Re-read immediately before writing to avoid overwriting intervening edits, and verify the saved spec by reading it back. Record the ticket URL and attached spec version/hash. If implementation later requires a material spec revision, repeat the affected review/readiness gate and refresh the ticket's accepted spec before resuming implementation. Missing Linear access or a failed attachment leaves this stage incomplete; report the concrete blocker.

## Stage 3: Implementation

Give the selected implementer the accepted spec, repository instructions, relevant code, and acceptance criteria. The selected implementer implements the scoped change and meaningful tests, runs the relevant checks, and reports deviations or unresolved issues. If implementation reveals a material flaw in the spec, return it to Astra for resolution and repeat the affected spec review before proceeding. A second related failure in one workflow is not another local patch: return it to Astra for the architectural root-cause check before expanding the fix.

The coordinator verifies the actual diff and test results. Passing tests alone does not demonstrate spec compliance.

The selected implementer fills the acceptance matrix with implementation file references and test names/results or appropriate manual evidence for every acceptance ID. Mark unmet or unverified criteria explicitly. Reviewers independently check the spec against implementation before comparing this matrix; the author's mapping is evidence to examine, not proof of coverage.

## Stage 4: Fable code review and Astra adjudication

Give a new Fable 5.1 session the accepted spec, base SHA, complete implementation diff, and surrounding code access. Request bugs, logical errors, architectural regressions, missing acceptance behavior, inadequate tests, and whether each affected transition has one canonical owner. Review callers and consumers beyond changed lines. Require severity, trigger, expected versus actual behavior, evidence, and a regression-test recommendation.

Astra validates findings against code and product intent. Reopen the architectural root-cause check when three related findings accumulate, or immediately for its high-risk triggers. Send accepted corrections to the selected implementer. Preserve a decision record for rejected findings with concrete reasons. Verify fixes and run affected tests. Obtain another Fable pass when corrections are substantial or its blocking concerns remain unresolved.

## Stage 5: Fresh Astra review

Start a completely new Astra context with high reasoning. Supply only the user request, accepted spec, repository instructions, base SHA, and current implementation snapshot. Do not seed it with earlier reviews, author explanations, adjudication records, or conversation history. Ask it to independently examine correctness, architecture, integration behavior, spec compliance, hidden duplicate ownership, implicit success inference, stale retry identity, and delayed-work reversals of terminal decisions in changed workflows.

After independent findings are returned, the coordinating Astra reconciles them with evidence and earlier decisions. The selected implementer implements accepted fixes and verifies them. Any substantive fix after this review requires a fresh focused Astra review of the affected behavior and its interactions. Record which final snapshot was reviewed; do not claim an earlier review covers later changes.

## Stage 6: Verify and publish

Confirm all required acceptance criteria are satisfied and substantive findings resolved. State whether the architectural root-cause check was triggered, its canonical-owner decision, and the tests covering delayed workers or connector sync, retry or recovery, cancellation, revocation, deletion, or replacement, and external-delivery uncertainty where relevant. Run repository-required checks and tests appropriate to the final diff. Report any checks that cannot run; do not describe them as passing. If a required review or correctness blocker remains, stop before publication unless the user explicitly requests a draft PR with those limitations.

Fetch the target branch again before publication and compare its current SHA with the recorded review base. Inspect intervening changes for overlapping code, callers, schemas, dependencies, and assumptions. Integrate relevant base changes using the repository's normal merge/rebase practice, preserving user work and avoiding force-pushes to shared branches. Have the selected implementer resolve implementation conflicts, with Astra deciding changes to behavior. Re-run affected checks and reviews for material changes. If the base advanced without affecting the feature, record the assessed SHA and reason integration was unnecessary. Record the final implementation commit and reviewed base in the handoff and PR; disclose if the remote moves again during publication.

Inspect the final diff, stage only the task's files, commit, and push the feature branch. Check for an existing PR for that branch and update it rather than creating a duplicate. Open a PR against the agreed base with the problem, resulting behavior, relevant design decisions, verification, and any migration requirements. Use a body file or structured API argument for multiline descriptions.

Finish with the Linear ticket and PR links, a concise account of the change, actual models used, review outcomes, test results, and remaining limitations. Leave merging and deployment to a separate user instruction.

## Stage 7: Close the Linear ticket after verified staging deployment

Keep the ticket **In Progress** while implementation, review, merge, or staging deployment is pending. After the feature's PR has been merged into `staging` and that exact merge/squash commit is verified as deployed to the staging environment, move the Linear ticket to **Done** with the bundled CLI's `set-state <IDENT> "Done"` command (resolve the team's actual Done workflow state first). Verify the PR's merged status and target branch using the hosting provider, confirm the commit is contained in remote `staging`, and verify the staging deployment identifies that commit or a descendant that includes it. A completed build, an open or merely closed PR, or a merge into `staging` before deployment verification does not satisfy this condition.

This closeout step does not authorize merging or deployment: retain the separate user instruction required for each. When both authorized operations complete, perform the ticket transition without another confirmation. On a resumed task, inspect the existing PR, staging deployment, and ticket before retrying. Read the ticket back to verify Done and report its URL and the merge and deployment evidence. If the state update fails, report that staging deployment completed but ticket closeout remains incomplete.

1	"""A deferred folder is settled only by listing its subtree, never by its metadata (AIO-1167 R51 final 1).
2	
3	Spec (accepted-spec AC-03/05/07; Astra 20:01 UTC adjudication, finding 1). A folder root whose read
4	was deferred while a snapshot was being built has only a placeholder in that build — retained
5	membership, none on fresh local state. Reading the folder's metadata later proves where it is, not
6	what is under it. Through the real coordinator over ``_DriveWorld``:
7	
8	  * with existing brain claims and FRESH local state, folder A deferred and the build kept open by a
9	    sibling larger than one run's discovery budget, a restart in which A's metadata recovers and the
10	    change feed is empty lists A AND its nested folder before any complete reconciliation; every
11	    complete snapshot holds A's documents, their claims survive, and the brain's last success does
12	    not move until the connection is genuinely complete;
13	  * with RETAINED local membership, a document under A that is gone at the provider (no change the
14	    stream can see) is NOT kept by the placeholder: the subtree is listed again and the complete
15	    snapshot retires its claim — never reported complete with stale membership;
16	  * a recovered listing interrupted part-way leaves A deferred and the connection incomplete; after a
17	    restart it resumes, lists the rest, settles A and completes.
18	
19	Post-blind corrections (Astra adjudication of Fable's R51 findings):
20	
21	  * F1 — ordinary uncertainty (a non-deferral metadata error, here on the change-page path) never
22	    erases A's deferred marker: it survives a reopened SQLite file, metadata recovery alone does not
23	    settle A, A and its nested folder are listed before any complete reconciliation, existing claims
24	    survive and last success waits for completion. Ordinary uncertainty on a root that was never
25	    deferred is still settled by metadata recovery (control);
26	  * F3 — a deferred folder whose placeholder already closed its traversal, then answering 404, is not
27	    read in that build: a controlled replacement snapshot decides it, so no complete reconciliation
28	    carries its stale placeholder membership, it is never listed, and only its unsupported membership
29	    disappears — the direct selection, the sibling root and another connection's claim stay.
30	"""

"""A deferred folder is settled only by listing its subtree, never by its metadata (AIO-1167 R51 final 1).

Spec (accepted-spec AC-03/05/07; Astra 20:01 UTC adjudication, finding 1). A folder root whose read
was deferred while a snapshot was being built has only a placeholder in that build — retained
membership, none on fresh local state. Reading the folder's metadata later proves where it is, not
what is under it. Through the real coordinator over ``_DriveWorld``:

  * with existing brain claims and FRESH local state, folder A deferred and the build kept open by a
    sibling larger than one run's discovery budget, a restart in which A's metadata recovers and the
    change feed is empty lists A AND its nested folder before any complete reconciliation; every
    complete snapshot holds A's documents, their claims survive, and the brain's last success does
    not move until the connection is genuinely complete;
  * with RETAINED local membership, a document under A that is gone at the provider (no change the
    stream can see) is NOT kept by the placeholder: the subtree is listed again and the complete
    snapshot retires its claim — never reported complete with stale membership;
  * a recovered listing interrupted part-way leaves A deferred and the connection incomplete; after a
    restart it resumes, lists the rest, settles A and completes.

Post-blind corrections (Astra adjudication of Fable's R51 findings):

  * F1 — ordinary uncertainty (a non-deferral metadata error, here on the change-page path) never
    erases A's deferred marker: it survives a reopened SQLite file, metadata recovery alone does not
    settle A, A and its nested folder are listed before any complete reconciliation, existing claims
    survive and last success waits for completion. Ordinary uncertainty on a root that was never
    deferred is still settled by metadata recovery (control);
  * F3 — a deferred folder whose placeholder already closed its traversal, then answering 404, is not
    read in that build: a controlled replacement snapshot decides it, so no complete reconciliation
    carries its stale placeholder membership, it is never listed, and only its unsupported membership
    disappears — the direct selection, the sibling root and another connection's claim stay.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from aios_ingest.gdrive_sync import _MAX_DISCOVERY_PAGES_PER_STREAM
from aios_ingest.state import ROOT_DEFERRED_PREFIX, StateStore
from test_document_restrictions import clock  # noqa: F401 (fixture)
from test_gdrive_upgrade import _SECOND_INTEGRATION, _ClaimLedger, _DriveWorld, _ProviderHttpError
from test_root_evidence_r49 import real_deferral

GEN = 9
DRIVE = "shared-a"
# More listings than one run may make, so a folder of this size keeps a snapshot building.
BIG = _MAX_DISCOVERY_PAGES_PER_STREAM + 5
A_DOCS = {"doc-a1", "doc-a2"}


def _world(monkeypatch, *, big_a: bool = False, big_b: bool = True):
    world = _DriveWorld(folder_ids=["folder-a", "folder-b"]).install(monkeypatch)
    world.ledger = _ClaimLedger()
    world.put("folder-a", drive=DRIVE, folder=True)
    world.put("folder-a-sub", drive=DRIVE, parent="folder-a", folder=True)
    world.put("doc-a1", drive=DRIVE, parent="folder-a")
    world.put("doc-a2", drive=DRIVE, parent="folder-a-sub")
    if big_a:
        for i in range(BIG):
            world.put(f"folder-a{i}", drive=DRIVE, parent="folder-a", folder=True)
            world.put(f"doc-ax{i}", drive=DRIVE, parent=f"folder-a{i}")
    world.put("folder-b", drive=DRIVE, folder=True)
    world.put("doc-b", drive=DRIVE, parent="folder-b")
    if big_b:
        for i in range(BIG):
            world.put(f"folder-b{i}", drive=DRIVE, parent="folder-b", folder=True)
            world.put(f"doc-b{i}", drive=DRIVE, parent=f"folder-b{i}")
    return world


async def _until_complete(world, state, limit: int = 40):
    summary = None
    for _ in range(limit):
        summary = await world.run(state)
        if summary.authoritative_complete:
            return summary
    raise AssertionError(f"not complete after {limit} runs: {summary}")


def _deferred(state, world) -> bool:
    return ("folder", "folder-a") in state.deferred_roots(world.integration_id, GEN, DRIVE)


def _listed(world, folder: str) -> bool:
    return ("list", DRIVE, folder) in world.calls


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_fresh_state_with_brain_claims_lists_the_recovered_folder_before_any_complete_snapshot(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, clock,
):
    world = _world(monkeypatch)
    first_state = StateStore(str(tmp_path / "first.sqlite"))
    await _until_complete(world, first_state)
    first_state.close()
    assert A_DOCS <= set(world.reconciled[-1])
    last_success = world.stream(DRIVE).get("last_success_at")

    # Fresh local state; folder A's read is deferred (a 503 naming no minimum).
    world.unreadable["folder-a"] = real_deferral(503)
    path = str(tmp_path / "fresh.sqlite")
    state = StateStore(path)
    world.calls.clear()
    await world.run(state)
    progress = state.get_progress(world.namespace(DRIVE))
    assert progress.building_snapshot is not None  # the sibling keeps this build open
    assert _deferred(state, world)
    assert not _listed(world, "folder-a")
    state.close()

    # Restart: A's metadata recovers; the change feed is empty.
    world.unreadable.pop("folder-a")
    state = StateStore(path)
    summary = None
    for _ in range(40):
        mark = len(world.reconciled)
        summary = await world.run(state)
        for snapshot in world.reconciled[mark:]:
            assert A_DOCS <= set(snapshot), "a complete snapshot without folder A's subtree"
            assert _listed(world, "folder-a") and _listed(world, "folder-a-sub")
        if summary.authoritative_complete:
            break
        assert world.stream(DRIVE).get("last_success_at") == last_success  # not before completion
    assert summary is not None and summary.authoritative_complete
    assert _listed(world, "folder-a") and _listed(world, "folder-a-sub")
    for doc in A_DOCS:
        assert world.ledger.claims[doc] == {world.integration_id}  # the existing claims survive
        assert doc not in world.ledger.deleted
    assert not _deferred(state, world)
    state.close()

    tmp_path, monkeypatch, clock,

    # doc-a2 is gone at the provider, with no change this stream can see; A becomes readable again.

    summary = None
    for _ in range(40):
        before = len(world.reconciled)
        summary = await world.run(state)
        for snapshot in world.reconciled[before:]:
            assert "doc-a2" not in snapshot, "complete with stale retained membership"
        if summary.authoritative_complete:
            break
    assert summary is not None and summary.authoritative_complete
    assert len(world.reconciled) > mark
    assert "doc-a1" in world.reconciled[-1] and "doc-a2" not in world.reconciled[-1]

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_an_interrupted_recovered_listing_keeps_the_folder_deferred_and_resumes_after_restart(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, clock,
):
    world = _world(monkeypatch, big_a=True, big_b=False)
    path = str(tmp_path / "interrupted.sqlite")

    # Folder A is deferred during a controlled rescan, which publishes without it.
    world.logs.setdefault(DRIVE, []).append({"fileId": "folder-b", "file": dict(world.files["folder-b"])})
    world.unreadable["folder-a"] = real_deferral(503)
    for _ in range(6):
        await world.run(state)

    assert not interrupted.authoritative_complete
    assert _deferred(state, world)

    state.close()

    state = StateStore(path)  # restart
    summary = await _until_complete(world, state)
    assert summary.authoritative_complete
    assert a_docs <= set(world.reconciled[-1])
    assert not _deferred(state, world)
    assert _listed(world, "folder-a")

3	Spec (accepted-spec AC-04; Astra 20:01 UTC adjudication, finding 3). A watch call answered 429, or 403
4	naming a quota reason, is the ACCOUNT's quota — classified and represented exactly as a polling
5	provider call (``sources.gdrive.quota_deferral``): the parsed Retry-After deadline unshortened, the

"""Watch creation and stop quota responses establish the account hold (AIO-1167 R51 final 3).

Spec (accepted-spec AC-04; Astra 20:01 UTC adjudication, finding 3). A watch call answered 429, or 403
naming a quota reason, is the ACCOUNT's quota — classified and represented exactly as a polling
provider call (``sources.gdrive.quota_deferral``): the parsed Retry-After deadline unshortened, the
bounded fallback for a missing/malformed header, the last-instant sentinel for an unrepresentable one.
Through the REAL watch manager translation and the real renewal sweep:

  * renewal journals the hold locally (monotonic, this verified account), publishes it through the
    shared restriction owner under the current fence/revision, and makes NO further watch creation
    or stop call for the account in that sweep — whether publication succeeds or fails;
  * a definitive quota-rejected creation retires that attempt only; the predecessor channel and every
    cursor are unchanged; a quota-rejected stop stays ``cleanup_pending`` with no attempt spent;
  * a reopened SQLite file, a fresh one restored from acknowledged progress, and polling at a later
    generation of the same account all honour the hold; renewal resumes after the deadline;
  * a failed acknowledgment keeps the local hold and the next sweep publishes it; under the
    uncertainty latch nothing is sent;
  * another credential's hold is neither adopted nor disturbed; a lapsed shorter hold is replaced and
    a later shorter one never shortens it;
  * an ordinary permission 403, a 404, a timeout-like 5xx are never account holds.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import copy
import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from aios_ingest import watch_renewal
from aios_ingest.brain_client import BrainError
from aios_ingest.connector_state import (
    RESTRICTION_KEYS, add_hold, apply_restriction_sections, parse_restriction_evidence, restriction_sections,
)
from aios_ingest.gdrive_sync import _restriction_standing, _standing_account_hold, run_gdrive_stream
from aios_ingest.sources.gdrive import LATEST_INSTANT
from aios_ingest.sources.gdrive_watch import ConfiguredGoogleDriveWatchManager, GoogleDriveWatchManager
from aios_ingest.state import StateStore, StreamKey
from aios_ingest.watch_lifecycle import (
    ACTIVE, CLEANUP_PENDING, DISPATCHED, RETIRED, UNCERTAIN, WatchQuotaLimited, WatchRefused, to_section,
)
import test_account_hold_before_streams as polling
from test_watch_lifecycle import ACCOUNT, INTEGRATION, SETTINGS, _Brain, _conn, _ms, _record

GEN = 3  # the generation the lifecycle brain double acquires
LONG = "99999999"


class _GoogleError(Exception):
    """A Google API error as the client raises it: status and headers on ``resp``, reasons parsed."""

    def __init__(self, status, retry_after=None, reason=None):
        super().__init__(f"HTTP {status}")
        self.resp = SimpleNamespace(
            status=status, headers={"Retry-After": retry_after} if retry_after is not None else {},
        )
        self.error_details = [{"reason": reason}] if reason else []


class _FakeDrive:
    """Google Drive's watch endpoints, scripted: each call takes the next scripted answer."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        self.watch_answers: list = []
        self.stop_answers: list = []

    def changes(self):
        drive = self

        class Changes:
            def watch(self, **kwargs):
                return _Request(drive, "watch", kwargs.get("driveId", "my-drive"), kwargs["body"])
        return Changes()

    def channels(self):
        drive = self

        class Channels:
            def stop(self, body):
                return _Request(drive, "stop", body["id"], body)
        return Channels()


class _Request:
    def __init__(self, drive, kind, target, body):
        self.drive, self.kind, self.target, self.body = drive, kind, target, body

    def execute(self, num_retries=0):
        self.drive.calls.append((self.kind, self.target))
        answers = self.drive.watch_answers if self.kind == "watch" else self.drive.stop_answers
        answer = answers.pop(0) if answers else None
        if isinstance(answer, Exception):
            raise answer
        if self.kind == "watch":
            return {
                "id": self.body["id"], "resourceId": f"res-{self.body['id']}",
                "expiration": _ms(timedelta(days=6)),
            }
        return {}


def _fake_drive(monkeypatch) -> _FakeDrive:
    fake = _FakeDrive()
    monkeypatch.setattr(GoogleDriveWatchManager, "_service", lambda self, deadline=None: fake)
    return fake


def _ns(drive_id):
    return StreamKey("demo", INTEGRATION, ACCOUNT, drive_id).namespace(GEN)


def _quota_brain(*, due: bool, cleanups: int = 2) -> _Brain:
    """Two streams; ``due``: my-drive's channel is due (a successor is created) and shared-x has
    none; otherwise both have channels that are not due. Plus ``cleanups`` channels to stop."""
    brain = _Brain()
    brain.progress["streams"] = {
        "my-drive": {"drive_id": "my-drive", "page_token": "cursor-my"},
        "shared-x": {"drive_id": "shared-x", "page_token": "cursor-x"},
    }
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    records = {
        "current": _record(
            ACTIVE, attempt_id="current", resource_id="res-current",
            expires_at=(now + (timedelta(minutes=5) if due else timedelta(days=6))).isoformat(),
        ),
    }
    if not due:
        records["current-x"] = _record(
            ACTIVE, attempt_id="current-x", resource_id="res-current-x", drive_id="shared-x",
            namespace=_ns("shared-x"), expires_at=(now + timedelta(days=6)).isoformat(),
        )
    for i in range(cleanups):
        records[f"old{i}"] = _record(
            CLEANUP_PENDING, attempt_id=f"old{i}", resource_id=f"res-old{i}",
            expires_at=(now + timedelta(days=5)).isoformat(),
        )
    brain.progress["watches"] = to_section(records)
    return brain


def _manager():
    return ConfiguredGoogleDriveWatchManager([_conn()])


def _hold(state, credential=ACCOUNT):
    return state.connection_hold(INTEGRATION, GEN, credential)


def _published_hold(brain, credential=ACCOUNT):
    entry = parse_restriction_evidence(brain.progress).get(credential) or {}
    return entry.get("hold")


def _near(instant: str, expected: datetime, tolerance: float = 120) -> bool:
    return abs((datetime.fromisoformat(instant) - expected).total_seconds()) < tolerance


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# The watch manager's error translation (real dispatch / stop, scripted transport)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #

def _direct_manager(monkeypatch):
    fake = _fake_drive(monkeypatch)
    return GoogleDriveWatchManager(webhook_url="https://example.test/watch", access_token="t"), fake


@pytest.mark.parametrize("answer", [
    pytest.param(lambda: _GoogleError(429, LONG), id="429"),
    pytest.param(lambda: _GoogleError(403, LONG, reason="rateLimitExceeded"), id="quota-403"),
])
def test_a_quota_answer_to_creation_or_stop_is_translated_with_its_deadline(monkeypatch, answer):
    manager, fake = _direct_manager(monkeypatch)
    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    fake.watch_answers = [answer()]
    with pytest.raises(WatchQuotaLimited) as created:
        manager.dispatch(_record(DISPATCHED), page_token="cursor", verification_token="token")
    fake.stop_answers = [answer()]
    with pytest.raises(WatchQuotaLimited) as stopped:
        manager.stop("old", "res-old")
    for raised in (created.value, stopped.value):
        assert raised.deferral.category == "rate_limited"
        assert raised.deferral.provider_deadline is True
        assert _near(raised.deferral.not_before, started + timedelta(seconds=int(LONG)))  # unshortened


@pytest.mark.parametrize("header, check", [
    ("soon", "fallback-malformed"), (None, "fallback"), ("9" * 30, "latest"),
])
def test_a_quota_answer_without_a_valid_retry_after_uses_the_established_representation(monkeypatch, header, check):
    manager, fake = _direct_manager(monkeypatch)
    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    fake.watch_answers = [_GoogleError(429, header)]
    with pytest.raises(WatchQuotaLimited) as raised:
        manager.dispatch(_record(DISPATCHED), page_token="cursor", verification_token="token")
    deferral = raised.value.deferral
    if check == "latest":
        assert deferral.not_before == LATEST_INSTANT.isoformat()
        assert deferral.diagnostic == "retry_after_unrepresentable"
    else:
        assert datetime.fromisoformat(deferral.not_before) <= started + timedelta(seconds=4.5)
        assert deferral.provider_deadline is False
        assert deferral.diagnostic == ("retry_after_malformed" if check == "fallback-malformed" else None)


def test_non_quota_answers_keep_their_existing_watch_outcomes(monkeypatch):
    manager, fake = _direct_manager(monkeypatch)
    fake.watch_answers = [_GoogleError(403)]  # a permission refusal names no quota reason
    with pytest.raises(WatchRefused):
        manager.dispatch(_record(DISPATCHED), page_token="cursor", verification_token="token")
    fake.watch_answers = [_GoogleError(500)]  # outcome unknown: raised as is
    with pytest.raises(_GoogleError):
        manager.dispatch(_record(DISPATCHED), page_token="cursor", verification_token="token")
    fake.stop_answers = [_GoogleError(404)]  # already gone
    assert manager.stop("old", "res-old") is None
    fake.stop_answers = [_GoogleError(403)]
    with pytest.raises(_GoogleError):
        manager.stop("old", "res-old")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Renewal learns the hold, stops, publishes — and every surface honours it
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ #

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_a_creation_quota_answer_holds_the_account_and_stops_every_further_watch_call(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch,
):
    fake = _fake_drive(monkeypatch)
    fake.watch_answers = [_GoogleError(429, LONG)]
    brain = _quota_brain(due=True).install(monkeypatch)
    streams_before = copy.deepcopy(brain.progress["streams"])
    path = str(tmp_path / "creation.sqlite")
    state = StateStore(path)
    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    await watch_renewal.renew_watches(state, _manager(), [_conn()], SETTINGS)

    # One creation — then no second creation and no stop.
    assert fake.calls == [("watch", "my-drive")]
    held = _hold(state)
    assert held is not None and _near(held[0], started + timedelta(seconds=int(LONG)))
    assert _published_hold(brain) is not None and _published_hold(brain)[0] == held[0]  # published
    records = brain.records()
    assert records["current"].state == ACTIVE  # the valid predecessor is untouched
    retired = [r for r in records.values() if r.state == RETIRED and r.predecessor == "current"]
    assert len(retired) == 1  # the definitive quota-rejected attempt retired, and nothing else
    assert all(records[f"old{i}"].state == CLEANUP_PENDING for i in range(2))
    assert all(records[f"old{i}"].stop_attempts == 0 for i in range(2))
    assert brain.progress["streams"] == streams_before  # no cursor moved
    assert brain.events[-1] == "release"
    state.close()

    # A reopened SQLite file and a fresh one restored from acknowledged progress: no watch call.
    for name in ("creation.sqlite", "fresh.sqlite"):
        fake.calls.clear()
        again = StateStore(str(tmp_path / name))
        await watch_renewal.renew_watches(again, _manager(), [_conn()], SETTINGS)
        assert fake.calls == []
        assert _hold(again) == held
        again.close()

    # After the deadline renewal resumes: the due creations and the pending stops are made.
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "aios_ingest.gdrive_sync._now",
        lambda: (datetime.fromisoformat(held[0]) + timedelta(seconds=1)).isoformat(),
    )
    fake.calls.clear()
    state = StateStore(path)
    await watch_renewal.renew_watches(state, _manager(), [_conn()], SETTINGS)
    assert ("watch", "my-drive") in fake.calls and ("watch", "shared-x") in fake.calls
    assert ("stop", "old0") in fake.calls
    state.close()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_a_stop_quota_answer_keeps_the_channel_cleanup_pending_and_holds_the_account(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    fake = _fake_drive(monkeypatch)
    fake.stop_answers = [_GoogleError(429, LONG)]
    brain = _quota_brain(due=False).install(monkeypatch)
    state = StateStore(str(tmp_path / "stop.sqlite"))

    await watch_renewal.renew_watches(state, _manager(), [_conn()], SETTINGS)

    assert fake.calls == [("stop", "old0")]  # the second stop is never attempted
    records = brain.records()
    assert records["old0"].state == CLEANUP_PENDING and records["old0"].stop_attempts == 0
    assert records["old1"].state == CLEANUP_PENDING and records["old1"].stop_attempts == 0
    assert records["current"].state == ACTIVE and records["current-x"].state == ACTIVE
    assert _hold(state) is not None and _published_hold(brain) is not None
    state.close()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_polling_at_a_later_generation_of_the_same_account_honours_the_watch_learned_hold(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch,
):
    fake = _fake_drive(monkeypatch)
    fake.watch_answers = [_GoogleError(429, LONG)]
    brain = _quota_brain(due=True).install(monkeypatch)

    """A lost acknowledgment: the brain stores the document, and its answer never arrives."""

    def fault(brain, payload):

@pytest.mark.parametrize("failure, stored, cancels", _RETIREMENT_FAILURES)
@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_a_creation_quota_hold_is_journaled_before_its_retirement_is_published(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, failure, stored, cancels,
):
    """R51 F2: the hold is in the local journal BEFORE the quota-rejected attempt's retirement is
    published, so a failed, refused, unacknowledged or cancelled publication cannot lose it. That
    publication's own outcome ends the connection run unchanged: nothing is projected as
    acknowledged, no further watch call is made, the lease is released — and the local hold alone
    blocks polling and renewal until a fresh acquisition publishes it."""
    fake = _fake_drive(monkeypatch)
    fake.watch_answers = [_GoogleError(429, LONG)]
    brain = _quota_brain(due=True)
    streams_before = copy.deepcopy(brain.progress["streams"])
    path = str(tmp_path / "retirement.sqlite")
    state = StateStore(path)
    held_at_checkpoint: list = []

    def at_quota_retirement(payload):
        records = (payload.get("watches") or {}).get("records") or []
        if not any(r.get("state") == RETIRED and r.get("detail") == "provider quota limited" for r in records):
            return None
        held_at_checkpoint.append(_hold(state))
        return failure(brain, payload)

    brain.checkpoint_faults.append(at_quota_retirement)
    brain.install(monkeypatch)
    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    if cancels:
        with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):  # propagated, never replaced by the hold
            await watch_renewal.renew_watches(state, _manager(), [_conn()], SETTINGS)
    else:
        await watch_renewal.renew_watches(state, _manager(), [_conn()], SETTINGS)

    # Journaled before the retirement checkpoint was even invoked, at the provider's deadline.
    assert len(held_at_checkpoint) == 1
    assert held_at_checkpoint[0] is not None
    assert _near(held_at_checkpoint[0][0], started + timedelta(seconds=int(LONG)))
    assert _hold(state) == held_at_checkpoint[0]
    # One creation — no second creation, no stop.
    assert fake.calls == [("watch", "my-drive")]
    assert _published_hold(brain) is None  # never claimed remote-durable
    records = brain.records()
    (attempt,) = [r for r in records.values() if r.predecessor == "current"]
    assert attempt.state == (RETIRED if stored else DISPATCHED)
    # The failed retirement is not projected locally as acknowledged.
    assert _local_watch_state(state, attempt.attempt_id) == DISPATCHED
    assert records["current"].state == ACTIVE  # the predecessor is untouched
    assert all(records[f"old{i}"].state == CLEANUP_PENDING for i in range(2))
    assert all(records[f"old{i}"].stop_attempts == 0 for i in range(2))
    assert brain.progress["streams"] == streams_before  # no cursor moved
    assert brain.events[-1] == "release"
    state.close()

    # Reopened: the local journal alone blocks polling's admission and renewal; the fresh acquisition
    # recovers the attempt without activating it and publishes the hold.
    state = StateStore(path)
    assert _standing_account_hold(state, INTEGRATION, GEN, ACCOUNT) is not None
    fake.calls.clear()
    await watch_renewal.renew_watches(state, _manager(), [_conn()], SETTINGS)
    assert fake.calls == []
    assert _published_hold(brain) is not None and _published_hold(brain)[0] == _hold(state)[0]
    records = brain.records()
    assert records[attempt.attempt_id].state in (UNCERTAIN, RETIRED)  # never active
    assert records[attempt.attempt_id].resource_id is None
    assert records["current"].state == ACTIVE
    assert all(records[f"old{i}"].state == CLEANUP_PENDING for i in range(2))
    assert all(records[f"old{i}"].stop_attempts == 0 for i in range(2))
    assert brain.progress["streams"] == streams_before
    assert brain.events[-1] == "release"
    state.close()

#   · ``uncertain`` — it WAS bound, and where it is now could not be read.
    #   · ``relocating`` — it was read in ``pending_drive_id``, whose stream has not taken it over.
    #
    # Every state but ``bound`` leaves the connection incomplete and is never absence evidence; a
    # selected root with no row at all is unknown, never resolved.
    def bind_root(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, root_kind: str, root_id: str, drive_id: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Record the drive that contains one selected root.

        The first binding stands; an ``unresolved`` obligation is the one row this resolves, so a
        retried binding lands on the obligation it was waiting on. ``drive_id`` must be a real drive.
        """
        if not drive_id:
            raise ValueError("a root binding needs the drive that was read for it")
        self._db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO selection_root_bindings(connection_id,generation,root_kind,root_id,drive_id) "
            "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?) ON CONFLICT(connection_id,generation,root_kind,root_id) DO UPDATE SET "
            "drive_id=excluded.drive_id,status='bound',pending_drive_id=NULL,detail=NULL,bound_at=? "
            "WHERE selection_root_bindings.status='unresolved'",
            (connection_id, generation, root_kind, root_id, drive_id, _now_iso()),
        )
        self._db.commit()

    def mark_root_unresolved(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, root_kind: str, root_id: str, *, detail: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Record that a selected root's INITIAL binding failed. It gets no drive.

        A root already bound (in any state) is never downgraded: what was read about it stands.
        """
        self._db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO selection_root_bindings(connection_id,generation,root_kind,root_id,drive_id,status,detail) "
            "VALUES(?,?,?,?,'','unresolved',?) ON CONFLICT(connection_id,generation,root_kind,root_id) DO UPDATE SET "
            "detail=excluded.detail WHERE selection_root_bindings.status='unresolved'",
            (connection_id, generation, root_kind, root_id, detail),
        )
        self._db.commit()

    def root_bindings(self, connection_id: str, generation: int) -> dict[tuple[str, str], str]:
        """The drive of every selected root whose drive is KNOWN. An unresolved root has none."""
        rows = self._db.execute(
            "SELECT root_kind,root_id,drive_id FROM selection_root_bindings "
            "WHERE connection_id=? AND generation=? AND status<>'unresolved'",
            (connection_id, generation),
        ).fetchall()
        return {(str(r["root_kind"]), str(r["root_id"])): str(r["drive_id"]) for r in rows}

    def root_obligations(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int,
    ) -> dict[tuple[str, str], RootBinding]:
        """Every selected-root obligation of a generation, in every state."""
        rows = self._db.execute(
            "SELECT root_kind,root_id,drive_id,status,pending_drive_id,detail FROM selection_root_bindings "
            "WHERE connection_id=? AND generation=? ORDER BY root_kind,root_id",
            (connection_id, generation),
        ).fetchall()
        return {
            (str(r["root_kind"]), str(r["root_id"])): RootBinding(
                str(r["drive_id"]), str(r["status"]), r["pending_drive_id"], r["detail"],
            )
            for r in rows
        }

    def restore_root_obligation(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, root_kind: str, root_id: str,
        binding: RootBinding,
    ) -> bool:
        """Adopt one obligation the brain acknowledged, when this state holds none for that root.

        Local evidence, where present, stands: this only fills in what a lost or older local state
        lacks. An obligation whose state is unknown, or a bound one with no drive, is not adopted.
        """
        if binding.status not in ROOT_STATES:
            return False
        if binding.status != "unresolved" and not binding.drive_id:
            return False
        if binding.status == "relocating" and not binding.pending_drive_id:
            return False
        cur = self._db.execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO selection_root_bindings"
            "(connection_id,generation,root_kind,root_id,drive_id,status,pending_drive_id,detail) "
            "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
            (connection_id, generation, root_kind, root_id,
             "" if binding.status == "unresolved" else binding.drive_id, binding.status,
             binding.pending_drive_id if binding.status == "relocating" else None, binding.detail),
        )
        self._db.commit()
        return cur.rowcount == 1

    def unknown_root_count(self, connection_id: str, generation: int) -> int:
        """Selected roots whose drive is unknown or unreadable now: either may hide a stream."""
        row = self._db.execute(
            "SELECT count(*) AS n FROM selection_root_bindings WHERE connection_id=? AND generation=? "
            "AND status IN ('unresolved','uncertain')",
            (connection_id, generation),
        ).fetchone()
        return int(row["n"])

    # A binding is ``bound`` while its root is known to live in ``drive_id``. The other states are
    # durable and all mean the connection is not complete: ``unresolved`` (above), ``uncertain`` —
    # where the root is now could not be read, so nothing is concluded about it — and ``relocating``
    # — it was read in ``pending_drive_id``, whose stream has not taken it over yet. None of them is
    # absence evidence.
    def unsettled_roots(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int,
    ) -> dict[tuple[str, str], RootBinding]:
        """Every selected root that is unresolved, uncertain or on its way to another drive."""
        rows = self._db.execute(
            "SELECT root_kind,root_id,drive_id,status,pending_drive_id,detail FROM selection_root_bindings "
            "WHERE connection_id=? AND generation=? AND status<>'bound' ORDER BY root_kind,root_id",
            (connection_id, generation),
        ).fetchall()
        return {
            (str(r["root_kind"]), str(r["root_id"])): RootBinding(
                str(r["drive_id"]), str(r["status"]), r["pending_drive_id"], r["detail"],
            )
            for r in rows
        }

    def mark_root_uncertain(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, root_kind: str, root_id: str, drive_id: str,
        *, detail: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Record that a root's location is unverified. A root already relocating stays that, and an
        unresolved one — never bound, so it has no drive to be uncertain about — stays unresolved.

        A DEFERRED root keeps its ``ROOT_DEFERRED_PREFIX`` detail (AIO-1167 R51 F1): ordinary
        uncertainty is not a listing, so it must not erase the enumeration debt that only a listing,
        a relocation/rebind or a verified not-found may discharge."""
        deferred = f"{ROOT_DEFERRED_PREFIX}%"
        self._db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO selection_root_bindings(connection_id,generation,root_kind,root_id,drive_id,status,detail) "
            "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,'uncertain',?) ON CONFLICT(connection_id,generation,root_kind,root_id) DO UPDATE SET "
            "status='uncertain',detail=CASE WHEN selection_root_bindings.status='uncertain' "
            "AND coalesce(selection_root_bindings.detail,'') LIKE ? "
            "AND coalesce(excluded.detail,'') NOT LIKE ? "
            "THEN selection_root_bindings.detail ELSE excluded.detail END "
            "WHERE selection_root_bindings.status NOT IN ('relocating','unresolved')",
            (connection_id, generation, root_kind, root_id, drive_id, detail, deferred, deferred),
        )
        self._db.commit()

    def mark_root_relocating(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, root_kind: str, root_id: str, drive_id: str,
        *, destination: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Record the drive a root was read in. It stays bound to ``drive_id`` until rebound.

        Only a root that was bound can relocate: an unresolved obligation is resolved by
        ``bind_root``, never by inventing the drive it supposedly left."""
        self._db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO selection_root_bindings(connection_id,generation,root_kind,root_id,drive_id,status,pending_drive_id,detail) "
            "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,'relocating',?,?) ON CONFLICT(connection_id,generation,root_kind,root_id) DO UPDATE SET "
            "status='relocating',pending_drive_id=excluded.pending_drive_id,detail=excluded.detail "
            "WHERE selection_root_bindings.status<>'unresolved'",
            (connection_id, generation, root_kind, root_id, drive_id, destination,
             f"observed in drive {destination}"),
        )
        self._db.commit()

    def settle_root(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, root_kind: str, root_id: str,
        *, enumerated: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """A root read where it is bound is no longer uncertain — nor unavailable (R48 D1): read
        again, it is restored. A relocation is never settled here.

        A DEFERRED root (``ROOT_DEFERRED_PREFIX``, AIO-1167 R50 F4) is different: its stream's
        snapshot holds only retained membership for it, so reading its metadata proves where it is,
        not what is under it. Only the enumeration that lists it again (``enumerated``) settles it."""
        self._db.execute(
            "UPDATE selection_root_bindings SET status='bound',detail=NULL WHERE connection_id=? "
            "AND generation=? AND root_kind=? AND root_id=? "
            "AND (status='uncertain' OR (status='bound' AND detail IS NOT NULL)) "
            "AND (? OR NOT (status='uncertain' AND coalesce(detail,'') LIKE ?))",
            (connection_id, generation, root_kind, root_id, 1 if enumerated else 0,
             f"{ROOT_DEFERRED_PREFIX}%"),
        )
        self._db.commit()

    def mark_root_deferred(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, root_kind: str, root_id: str, drive_id: str,
        *, detail: str,
    ) -> None:
        """Record that a bound root could not be read by its stream's enumeration now (R50 F4): a
        provider minimum or a non-quota deferral. It becomes ``uncertain`` with a
        ``ROOT_DEFERRED_PREFIX`` detail — a durable unresolved obligation that keeps the connection
        partial and withholds absence — until an enumeration lists it again."""
        self.mark_root_uncertain(
            connection_id, generation, root_kind, root_id, drive_id,
            detail=f"{ROOT_DEFERRED_PREFIX}: {detail}",
        )

    def deferred_roots(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, drive_id: str,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        """``(kind, id)`` of every root of this drive's stream deferred by its enumeration."""
        return [
            (str(row["root_kind"]), str(row["root_id"]))
            for row in self._db.execute(
                "SELECT root_kind,root_id FROM selection_root_bindings WHERE connection_id=? "
                "AND generation=? AND drive_id=? AND status='uncertain' AND coalesce(detail,'') LIKE ? "
                "ORDER BY root_kind,root_id",
                (connection_id, generation, drive_id, f"{ROOT_DEFERRED_PREFIX}%"),
            ).fetchall()
        ]

    def record_root_unavailable(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, root_kind: str, root_id: str, *, detail: str,
    ) -> bool:
        """Record a previously BOUND root's own verified not-found (AIO-1167 R48 D1).

        The root stays bound to its drive — its location was known and its outcome is now known:
        it supports nothing — with the diagnostic as its detail, which travels with the fenced
        root evidence. Only a bound (or uncertain) root qualifies: a never-bound root stays
        unresolved and a relocating one stays relocating; neither is evidence of loss. Returns
        whether the root was recorded."""
        cur = self._db.execute(
            "UPDATE selection_root_bindings SET status='bound',detail=? WHERE connection_id=? "
            "AND generation=? AND root_kind=? AND root_id=? AND status IN ('bound','uncertain') "
            "AND drive_id IS NOT NULL AND drive_id<>''",
            (detail, connection_id, generation, root_kind, root_id),
        )
        self._db.commit()
        return cur.rowcount == 1

    def rebind_root(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, root_kind: str, root_id: str, destination: str,
    ) -> bool:
        """Hand a relocating root to the stream of the drive it was read in, atomically."""
        cur = self._db.execute(
            "UPDATE selection_root_bindings SET drive_id=pending_drive_id,status='bound',"
            "pending_drive_id=NULL,detail=NULL,bound_at=? WHERE connection_id=? AND generation=? "
            "AND root_kind=? AND root_id=? AND status='relocating' AND pending_drive_id=?",
            (_now_iso(), connection_id, generation, root_kind, root_id, destination),
        )
        self._db.commit()
        return cur.rowcount == 1

    def cancel_relocation(
        self, connection_id: str, generation: int, root_kind: str, root_id: str,
    ) -> bool:
        """A relocating root read back in the drive it is bound to never left that stream."""
        cur = self._db.execute(
            "UPDATE selection_root_bindings SET status='bound',pending_drive_id=NULL,detail=NULL "
            "WHERE connection_id=? AND generation=? AND root_kind=? AND root_id=? AND status='relocating'",
            (connection_id, generation, root_kind, root_id),
        )
        self._db.commit()
        return cur.rowcount == 1

def _deferred_root_admissible(
    state: StateStore, execution: GdriveExecution, options: dict[str, Any], generation: int,
    drive_id: str,
    *,
    source: GoogleDriveSource | None = None,
    probed: set[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
    diagnostics: IngestSummary | None = None,
) -> bool:
    """Whether a controlled rescan should start because a root this drive's enumeration deferred
    (R50 F4) may be read again.

    A root under a standing provider minimum is never read early: it cannot authorize a rescan. Any
    other deferred root first gets a bounded ROOT-LOCAL probe (R51 F4) — one metadata read through
    the existing provider gate, deadline and retry contract, at most once per root per run
    (``probed``, owned by the coordinator) — so a root that keeps timing out does not relist its
    healthy siblings on every poll:

      * a quota answer is the account's hold (raised);
      * the run's own budget ends probing for this run, the rescan not started;
      * any other deferral keeps the root deferred, records a newly named provider minimum, and
        the stream's independent changes drain without a rescan;
      * an answer that locates the root (present here, elsewhere, or verified not-found) only
        AUTHORIZES the normal controlled rescan, whose own evidence paths decide; the probe never
        settles the root nor establishes membership.

    With no ``source`` (no probe possible) the pre-R51 rule applies: any unrestricted deferred root."""
    deferred = state.deferred_roots(execution.integration_id, generation, drive_id)
    if not deferred:
        return False
    credential = credential_identity(options)
    restricted = set(_standing_document_restrictions(
        state, execution.integration_id, generation, credential,
    ))
    eligible = [(kind, root_id) for kind, root_id in deferred if root_id not in restricted]
    if not eligible:
        return False
    if source is None:
        return True
    probed = probed if probed is not None else set()
    report = diagnostics if diagnostics is not None else IngestSummary("probe", failure_categories={})
    for kind, root_id in eligible:
        if (kind, root_id) in probed:
            continue
        probed.add((kind, root_id))
        try:
            observed = _observe_root(source, root_id, drive_id, {})
        except ProviderDeferred as exc:
            if exc.category == "rate_limited":
                raise _account_hold(exc) from exc
            _count(report, exc.category)
            _count_retry_after_diagnostic(report, exc)
            if exc.category in _LOCAL_DEADLINE_CATEGORIES:
                return False
            _restrict_resource(state, execution, credential, root_id, exc)

149	@dataclass
150	class _Run:
151	    """One connection's renewal: its deadline, its fenced publication and its workers."""
152	
153	    client: BrainClient
154	    execution: Any
155	    state: StateStore
156	    team: str
157	    deadline: float
158	    records: dict[str, WatchRecord]
159	    running: list[Future] = field(default_factory=list)
160	
161	    def remaining(self) -> float:
162	        return self.deadline - time.monotonic()
163	
164	    async def bounded(self, awaitable: Any) -> Any:
165	        remaining = self.remaining()
166	        if remaining <= 0:
167	            if asyncio.iscoroutine(awaitable):
168	                awaitable.close()
169	            raise WatchStepTimeout(started=False)
170	        try:
171	            return await asyncio.wait_for(awaitable, timeout=remaining)
172	        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
173	            raise WatchStepTimeout(started=True) from None
174	
175	    async def offload(
176	        self, fn: Callable[[], Any], *, on_late: Callable[[Future], None] | None = None,
177	        deadline: float | None = None,
178	    ) -> Any:
179	        """Run one blocking step in the owned pool, bounded by ``deadline`` (default: the run's).
180	
181	        A step that never started is cancelled outright — nothing was done. A step already running
182	        cannot be interrupted: it is abandoned, its outcome handed to ``on_late`` (from its own
183	        thread) and its resources kept open until it ends. Cancellation of this coroutine is never
184	        swallowed.
185	        """
186	        remaining = (deadline if deadline is not None else self.deadline) - time.monotonic()
187	        if remaining <= 0:
188	            raise WatchStepTimeout(started=False)
189	        future = _POOL.submit(fn)
190	        self.running.append(future)
191	        future.add_done_callback(lambda done: self.running.remove(done) if done in self.running else None)
192	        try:
193	            return await _wait_bounded(asyncio.shield(asyncio.wrap_future(future)), remaining)
194	        except (asyncio.TimeoutError, asyncio.CancelledError) as exc:
195	            started = not future.cancel()
196	            if started and on_late is not None:
197	                future.add_done_callback(on_late)
198	            if isinstance(exc, asyncio.CancelledError):
199	                raise
200	            raise WatchStepTimeout(started=started) from None
201	
202	    async def publish(self, *changed: WatchRecord) -> None:
203	        """Publish lifecycle changes under the fence, then project them locally.
204	
205	        Raises when the brain refuses (stale authority) or cannot be reached in time: nothing is
206	        projected then, and the next sweep starts again from what the brain holds.
207	        """
208	        updated = dict(self.records)
209	        for record in changed:
210	            updated[record.attempt_id] = record
211	        document = renewal_document(self.execution.progress, to_section(updated))
212	        ack = await self.bounded(self.client.checkpoint_gdrive_execution(self.execution, document)) or {}
213	        acknowledged = dict(ack.get("progress") or document)
214	        self.execution.progress.clear()
215	        self.execution.progress.update(acknowledged)
216	        self.records = updated
217	        for record in changed:
218	            self.state.save_watch_record(record)

221	def _close_when_idle(run: _Run | None, closers: list[Callable[[], None]]) -> None:
222	    """Close shared resources now, or once the last abandoned worker using them has finished."""
223	    pending = [future for future in (run.running if run else []) if not future.done()]
224	    lock = threading.Lock()
225	    closed = [False]
226	
227	    def close_all(*_args: Any) -> None:
228	        if any(not future.done() for future in pending):
229	            return
230	        with lock:
231	            if closed[0]:
232	                return
233	            closed[0] = True
234	        for close in closers:
235	            try:
236	                close()
237	            except Exception:
238	                pass
239	
240	    if not pending:
241	        close_all()
242	        return
243	    for future in pending:
244	        future.add_done_callback(close_all)

247	def _late_evidence(
248	    loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, state: StateStore, record: WatchRecord,
249	) -> Callable[[Future], None]:
250	    """What an abandoned creation worker's eventual result may do: record cleanup evidence.
251	
252	    It runs in the worker's thread, so the SQLite write is handed back to the event loop. A late
253	    response can show that a channel exists (and how to stop it); it can never activate one.
254	    """
255	    def deliver(future: Future) -> None:
256	        if future.cancelled() or future.exception() is not None:
257	            return
258	        response = future.result()
259	        resource_id = response.get("resourceId") if isinstance(response, dict) else None
260	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
261	            return
262	        try:
263	            loop.call_soon_threadsafe(
264	                state.record_watch_evidence, record.connection, record.attempt_id, resource_id,
265	            )
266	        except RuntimeError:  # the loop is gone; the record stays uncertain until its expiry
267	            pass
268	    return deliver

276	async def _recover(run: _Run, connection: str, now: datetime) -> None:
277	    changed: list[WatchRecord] = []
278	    for record in sorted(run.records.values(), key=lambda r: r.attempt_id):
279	        if record.connection != connection or record.terminal:
280	            continue
281	        if record.state == PREPARED:
282	            # Never marked dispatched under the fence, so it was never sent.
283	            changed.append(transition(record, RETIRED, detail="intent abandoned before dispatch"))
284	        elif record.state == DISPATCHED:
285	            # This sweep holds the lease, so the worker that dispatched it is gone without a
286	            # published outcome: the channel may exist — and if Google has already named its
287	            # resource (early notification, late response), it does, and is stopped.
288	            evidence = run.state.watch_evidence(record.connection, record.attempt_id)
289	            if evidence:
290	                changed.append(transition(
291	                    record, CLEANUP_PENDING, resource_id=evidence,
292	                    detail="observed after its outcome was lost; stopping",
293	                ))
294	            else:
295	                changed.append(transition(record, UNCERTAIN, detail="dispatch outcome lost"))
296	        elif record.state == UNCERTAIN:
297	            evidence = run.state.watch_evidence(record.connection, record.attempt_id)
298	            if evidence:
299	                changed.append(transition(
300	                    record, CLEANUP_PENDING, resource_id=evidence,
301	                    detail="observed after an unknown outcome; stopping",
302	                ))
303	            elif _past(record.requested_expiry, now):
304	                changed.append(transition(record, EXPIRED, detail="past its requested expiry"))
305	        elif record.state in (ACTIVE, CLEANUP_PENDING) and _past(record.life_bound(), now):
306	            changed.append(transition(record, EXPIRED, detail="past its expiry"))
307	    if changed:
308	        await run.publish(*changed)

def begin_selection_snapshot(
        self, namespace: str, generation: int, roots: list[tuple[str, str, str, bool]],
    ) -> int:
        """Atomically create a replacement incarnation with roots and traversal seeds.

        The prior active incarnation remains readable until :meth:`publish_selection_snapshot`.
        Repeated calls while a build exists return that build and repair any missing seeds: the
        build is resumed under the start token it was begun with. A token captured since is not
        that token — see :meth:`restart_selection_snapshot`.
        """
        return self._open_selection_snapshot(namespace, generation, roots)

    def restart_selection_snapshot(
        self, namespace: str, generation: int, roots: list[tuple[str, str, str, bool]],
        *, start_token: str,
    ) -> int:
        """Atomically begin a new incarnation under a start token captured just now.

        What an unfinished build listed is no evidence for this token: a document that entered a
        folder after that folder was listed and before the token was captured is in neither the
        listing nor the changes after the token. So nothing is resumed. In one transaction the
        build is superseded — never enumerated or published again — a new incarnation is seeded
        with every root unlisted, each page still uncommitted is retired without moving the
        cursor, and the stream's cursor becomes this token in a new drain observation with no
        terminal evidence. The published membership stays authoritative, the superseded build
        still claims what it listed, and every document obligation stays owed, until the
        replacement is published — :meth:`publish_selection_snapshot` then ends the upserts owed
        for documents the replacement does not hold.
        """
        if not start_token:
            raise ValueError("a restarted snapshot needs the start token it is enumerated under")
        return self._open_selection_snapshot(namespace, generation, roots, start_token=start_token)

    def _open_selection_snapshot(
        self, namespace: str, generation: int, roots: list[tuple[str, str, str, bool]],
        *, start_token: str | None = None,
    ) -> int:
        self._db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            progress = self._db.execute(
                "SELECT building_snapshot FROM stream_progress WHERE namespace=?",
                (namespace,),
            ).fetchone()
            if start_token is not None:
                if progress is None:
                    raise KeyError(f"unknown stream namespace {namespace}")
                self._db.execute(
                    "UPDATE selection_snapshots SET status='superseded' "
                    "WHERE namespace=? AND generation=? AND status='building'",
                    (namespace, generation),
                )
                # A page read before this token is settled by the baseline that follows it, not by
                # its own continuation: retired here, it can neither advance the cursor nor wait on
                # a rescan that will never publish. The work it still owes is not touched.
                self._db.execute(
                    "DELETE FROM pending_work WHERE namespace=? AND generation=? "
                    "AND acknowledged_at IS NOT NULL AND page_id IN ("
                    "SELECT page_id FROM materialized_pages WHERE namespace=? AND generation=? "
                    "AND committed_at IS NULL)",
                    (namespace, generation, namespace, generation),
                )
                self._db.execute(
                    "UPDATE materialized_pages SET committed_at=? "
                    "WHERE namespace=? AND generation=? AND committed_at IS NULL",
                    (_now_iso(), namespace, generation),
                )
            resumed = progress[0] if progress and start_token is None else None
            snapshot_id = int(resumed) if resumed is not None else int(
                self._db.execute(
                    "SELECT coalesce(max(snapshot_id),0)+1 FROM ("
                    "SELECT snapshot_id FROM selection_snapshots WHERE namespace=? AND generation=? "
                    "UNION ALL SELECT snapshot_id FROM selected_membership WHERE namespace=? AND generation=? "
                    "UNION ALL SELECT snapshot_id FROM selection_roots WHERE namespace=? AND generation=? "
                    "UNION ALL SELECT snapshot_id FROM traversal_queue WHERE namespace=? AND generation=?"
                    ")",
                    (namespace, generation, namespace, generation, namespace, generation,
                     namespace, generation),
                ).fetchone()[0]
            )
            self._db.execute(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO selection_snapshots(namespace,generation,snapshot_id,status) "
                "VALUES(?,?,?,'building')",
                (namespace, generation, snapshot_id),
            )
            for root_id, kind, drive_id, recursive in roots:
                self._db.execute(
                    "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO selection_roots(namespace,generation,snapshot_id,root_id,root_kind,drive_id,recursive) "
                    "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                    (namespace, generation, snapshot_id, root_id, kind, drive_id, int(recursive)),
                )
                if kind in {"folder", "drive"}:
                    self._db.execute(
                        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO traversal_queue(namespace,generation,snapshot_id,root_id,folder_id,drive_id,page_token) "
                        "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                        (namespace, generation, snapshot_id, root_id,
                         drive_id if kind == "drive" else root_id, drive_id, ""),
                    )
                    seed_folder = drive_id if kind == "drive" else root_id
                    self._db.execute(
                        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO traversal_ancestry(namespace,generation,snapshot_id,root_id,folder_id,ancestor_id) "
                        "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                        (namespace, generation, snapshot_id, root_id, seed_folder, seed_folder),
                    )
            self._db.execute(
                "UPDATE stream_progress SET building_snapshot=?,listing_complete=0,phase='baselining',"
                "terminal_drain_token=NULL,terminal_drain_checkpoint_id=NULL,"
                "terminal_drain_acknowledged=0,terminal_drain_observation=NULL,updated_at=? "
                "WHERE namespace=?",
                (snapshot_id, _now_iso(), namespace),
            )
            if start_token is not None:
                # The new observation keeps every change page read from this token distinct from
                # any page read before it, even one read from an equal token.
                self._db.execute(
                    "UPDATE stream_progress SET baseline_start_token=?,page_token=NULL,"
                    "drain_observation=drain_observation+1 WHERE namespace=?",
                    (start_token, namespace),
                )
            self._db.commit()
            return snapshot_id
        except Exception:
            self._db.rollback()
            raise

    def replace_roots(self, namespace: str, generation: int,
                      roots: list[tuple[str, str, str, bool]]) -> None:
        self.begin_selection_snapshot(namespace, generation, roots)

    def snapshot_id(self, namespace: str, *, building: bool = True) -> int | None:
        row = self._db.execute(
            "SELECT active_snapshot,building_snapshot FROM stream_progress WHERE namespace=?",
            (namespace,),
        ).fetchone()
        if not row:
            return None
        selected = row["building_snapshot"] if building and row["building_snapshot"] is not None else row["active_snapshot"]
        # Compatibility for callers/tests that predate explicit snapshot initialization. The
        # coordinator always calls begin_selection_snapshot before provider enumeration.
        return int(selected) if selected is not None else 1

    def list_roots(self, namespace: str, generation: int,
                   *, snapshot_id: int | None = None) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        selected = snapshot_id if snapshot_id is not None else self.snapshot_id(namespace)
        if selected is None:
            return []
        return self._db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM selection_roots WHERE namespace=? AND generation=? AND snapshot_id=? "
            "ORDER BY root_kind,root_id",
            (namespace, generation, selected),
        ).fetchall()

    def enqueue_traversal(
        self, namespace: str, generation: int, root_id: str, folder_id: str,
        drive_id: str, page_token: str | None = None, *, snapshot_id: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        selected = snapshot_id if snapshot_id is not None else self.snapshot_id(namespace)
        if selected is None:
            raise RuntimeError("selection snapshot is not initialized")
        self._db.execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO traversal_queue(namespace,generation,snapshot_id,root_id,folder_id,drive_id,page_token) "
            "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
            (namespace, generation, selected, root_id, folder_id, drive_id, page_token or ""),
        )
        self._db.commit()

    def next_traversal(self, namespace: str, generation: int,
                       *, snapshot_id: int | None = None) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        selected = snapshot_id if snapshot_id is not None else self.snapshot_id(namespace)
        if selected is None:
            return None
